bridges.description: A contingent universe requires a necessary divine explanation.
Fine-tuning is best explained by design.
Theism grounds moral value, meaning, and purpose.
An absolute beginning is best explained by a personal creator.
Consciousness and basic mental causation support an ultimate mind.
Appropriately reasoned atheism can constitute knowledge.
Theism is weak against naturalistic background knowledge.
Ordinary causal intuitions may fail at cosmic origin.
Moral judgment need not imply divine grounding.
Reports and ordinary history do not establish miracles.
A cosmic cause does not by itself yield divine personal attributes.
